newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INTERVIEW-De Boer Unigro focuses on merger, Spain.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-De Boer Unigro focuses on merger, Spain.

text.p: De Boer Unigro, the second biggest Dutch supermarket chain, is trying to marry its domestic restructuring programme with overseas expansion, chairman Robert Ter Haar said on Tuesday.
"In the Netherlands, we're focusing on the integration of our different formulas. At the same time, we're actively looking for expansion in Spain," Ter Haar told Reuters in an interview.
At home, the company, which resulted from the merger of De Boer Winkelbedrijven and unlisted Unigro in May, is trying to harmonize the product ranges of its two flagship Dutch chains.
This should be completed by the start of next year.
"In the autumn of this year, the consumer will see the first signals of the new, integrated, formulas," Ter Haar said.

According to the chief financial officer Wouter Kranenburg, the benefits of integration would be felt soon, generating 15 million guilders of savings and synergy benefits in its second year, growing to about 30 million a year after five years.
"We'll invest part of that money in the improvement of brand awareness and of our distribution," Ter Haar said.
De Boer Unigro had a pro-forma net profit of 90.1 million guilders or 8.48 guilders per share in 1996, when turnover totalled 6.4 billion guilders.
The company, which will release its first combined half-year figures on August 26, has forecast average annual profit growth of at least 10 percent.
Further growth of De Boer Unigro at home -- where it has a 13 percent market share behind Ahold unit Albert Heijn, with 28 percent -- will come from acquisitions, Ter Haar said.
"You can't really beef up market share here by pure organic growth anymore," he said.
Kranenburg added the combine's improved financial position and brand awareness would give it room to make further Dutch acquisitions in the longer term.
But he said the first purchases would be made in Spain, where the company already has a major presence through its El Arbol supermarket chain.
De Boer Unigro intends to double turnover of its Spanish activities to 2.5 million guilders within five years.
"The major part of this will come from acquisitions, but we're also opening new stores at a high speed," Kranenburg said.
Some 30 stores will be opened this year in Spain, he said, which if continued at the same pace, would result in organic growth at a rate of several percent per year.
Ter Haar said the firm was looking to buy family or privately-owned chains with turnover between 50 and 250 million guilders in or near regions where it was already present.
"There have to be instant synergy benefits, and it has to contribute to earnings per share from year one," he said.

Kranenburg added the market share enjoyed by the Spanish chain, varying from seven to 20 percent in regions where active, was sufficient to assume a leading position due to the fragmented nature of the Spanish market.
And because wholesale suppliers are willing to offer more credit facilities than in the Netherlands, the return on net assets is much higher, he added.
